name: Scopa
description: Scopa is an Italian fishing card game where players capture table cards by matching rank or sum; points for sweeps, most cards, coins suit, sette bello and prime. First to 11+ points wins.

overview.description: Scopa is an Italian fishing card game where players capture table cards by matching rank or sum; points for sweeps, most cards, coins suit, sette bello and prime. First to 11+ points wins.

history.origins:
Country/Region of Origin: Italy
Time Period: 18th century (popular in Naples); roots in 15th-century Spanish games in Naples
Historical Development: Evolved from Spanish games Primero and Scarabucion in Naples port area; one of three major national card games in Italy with Briscola and Tresette
Cultural Significance: Popular social and family game in Italy; spread to Argentina, Brazil, and former Italian colonies via diaspora
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.players:
Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 2 or 4 (partnerships)
Partnerships: Optional for 4 or 6 players
setup.deck:
Type: 40-card Italian or stripped 52-card deck (no 8s, 9s, 10s). Suits: coins, cups, swords, batons (Latin) or diamonds, hearts, clubs, spades (French). Ranks: King=10, Horse/Queen=9, Jack=8, 7–2 face value, Ace=1.
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
setup.dealing: Three cards to each player, then four cards face up to the table; deal one at a time. After each round of three plays, deal three more to each player (no new table cards). Direction: counter-clockwise with 3+ players.

rules.objective: Capture cards from the table by matching rank or by matching the sum of two or more table cards; score points for sweeps (scopa), most cards, most coins/diamonds, the seven of coins (settebello), and the best primiera; first to 11 or more points wins the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal: Each player receives three cards; four cards are dealt face up to the table; remaining cards form the stock.
2. Play: Non-dealer plays first. On each turn, play one card from hand. If it matches a single table card by value, capture that card; if it equals the sum of two or more table cards, capture that set; otherwise leave the played card on the table. When you capture all table cards (sweep), that is a scopa and scores 1 point.
3. After each player has played three cards, the dealer gives three more cards to each player (no new table cards). Repeat until all cards are played.
4. End of hand: Remaining table cards go to the last captor. Score for scope, most cards, most coins, settebello, and best primiera. First to 11+ points wins.
keyRules: Capture by matching one table card's value or the sum of multiple table cards; if both options exist, you must take the single card.
Capturing is compulsory when possible; you may choose to play a card that does not capture only when it cannot capture.
Sweeping all table cards (scopa) scores 1 point; dealer's last card of the hand never counts as a scopa.
At end of hand, score 1 point each for: most cards, most coins/diamonds, having the seven of coins, and best primiera (one card per suit using Seven=21, Six=18, Ace=16, etc.).

strategy.basic: Capture when you can; prefer taking coins/diamonds and high primiera cards (sevens, sixes, aces). Avoid leaving table cards that let the next player make a scopa.
strategy.intermediate: Track which coins and high cards have been played; delay or force sweeps to deny the opponent scope; when choosing between captures, take the set that improves your primiera or coin count.
strategy.advanced: Set up sweeps for yourself by leaving sums that only your hand can make; block opponent sweeps by taking key cards or playing a card that forces a non-sweep capture; in primiera, prioritise capturing aces and sixes.
tips: The seven of coins (settebello) is worth one point and is key for primiera; try to capture it.
If you can capture with a single card or a set, you must take the single card; use this rule when it helps you.
Leaving the table empty after your capture (scopa) scores a point and can disrupt the opponent's plans.

variations.name: Asso Pigliatutto
variations.description: Playing an Ace captures all table cards (and scores a scopa) unless an Ace is on the table, in which case only the Ace is captured. Ace on empty table stays on table.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Scopa d'Assi
variations.description: Like Asso Pigliatutto except capturing all cards with an Ace does not count as a scopa. Often played with four players (Scopone-style) with 9 or 10 cards each.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Rule change only; no engine constant overrides.

variations.name: Scopa di Quindici
variations.description: Capture only when the played card plus captured card(s) sum to 15 (e.g. play 4 to take 4+5+6). Popular in Argentina and Brazil. Some versions also allow equal-value capture.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Capture rule change; no engine constant overrides.

scoring.description: One point per scopa (sweep); one point each for most cards, most coins/diamonds, seven of coins (settebello), and best primiera. First to 11 or more points wins.
scoring.winCondition: First player or team to reach 11 or more points after a hand wins the game; if tied, play another hand to break the tie.
